Note::TexAccessor::headings¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::headings(std::int64_t max_depth) const

Extract A Bounded Document Outline¶

headings(max_depth) extracts the required title argument from structural heading commands, up to an explicit outline depth. Commands and outer braces are omitted; balanced content inside the title is retained. Both numbered and starred forms are recognized, and an optional short title is skipped in favor of the required long title because the latter is the document heading readers see.

Depth describes hierarchy, not result count:

max_depth

Included commands

1

\part, \chapter, \section

2

depth 1 plus \subsection

3

depths 1–2 plus \subsubsection

4

depths 1–3 plus \paragraph

part, chapter, and section share depth 1 so the same call extracts the top-level outline from article- and book-shaped sources. The parameter must be in [1, 4]; zero, negative values, and values above four are rejected. It does not cap how many headings are returned.

Matching observes control-word boundaries. \sectioned is not a section, and an escaped \\section does not begin a heading. Optional and required groups must balance; malformed candidates are ignored rather than returned in part. The method does not expand title macros, render formatting commands, infer a hierarchy from document order, or validate whether a command is legal for a particular document class.

The output is a TokenBatch: flat Text tokens() retain lane and source order, while Int64 offsets() assign token ranges to receiver cells. Receiver rank is not lost: a rank-two Note with four cells still has five boundaries. Undefined input returns undefined tokens and offsets [0]; defined non-Text input is rejected. Work is linear in bytes scanned and title bytes copied.

Example 1: Select Top-Level Headings¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(\part{Front} \chapter{Start} \section[Short]{Top {title}})",
        R"(\subsection*{Detail} \subsubsection{Deep} \paragraph{Leaf})",
        R"(\sectioned{not a heading} \\section{escaped})", "plain"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto top = source.tex().headings(1);

std::cout << top.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Front", "Start", "Top {title}"]

The optional title Short is metadata, so the extracted title is Top {title}. Nested braces remain balanced content.

Example 2: Widen The Outline¶

for (const std::int64_t depth : {2, 4}) {
  const auto outline = source.tex().headings(depth);
  std::cout << "depth=" << depth << ' ' << outline.tokens() << '\n';
}

Output¶

depth=2 Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["Front", "Start", "Top {title}", "Detail"]
depth=4 Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["Front", "Start", "Top {title}", "Detail", "Deep", "Leaf"]

Example 3: Map The Full Outline Back To A Grid¶

const auto outline = source.tex().headings(4);
std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = outline.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 3, 6, 6, 6]

The first row’s two cells each own three headings. The second row contributes none, but its two cells remain represented by repeated boundaries.

Example 4: Reject Invalid Depths¶

for (const std::int64_t depth : {0, 5}) {
  try {
    (void)source.tex().headings(depth);
  } catch (const pluss::Error&) {
    std::cout << "headings(" << depth << "): rejected\n";
  }
}

Output¶

headings(0): rejected
headings(5): rejected

Example 5: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().headings(2);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().headings(2);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "headings Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
headings Int64: rejected
